None of the three solutions gives the correct value. The substitution in Solution 3 is valid and reduces the integral to $I=\int_0^{1/\sqrt3}\frac{\arctan(1/\sqrt{2-t^2})}{1+t^2}\,dt$, but the claimed value of $I$ is wrong. Simpson's rule on this reduced form gives $I\approx 0.32898$, which matches $\pi^2/30\approx 0.32899$ (the closed form I'd expect, though I haven't proven it). The three proposed answers are $\pi/10\approx0.3142$, $\pi/12\approx0.2618$, and $\pi^2/32\approx0.3084$.

CHOICE: NONE
CONFIDENCE: 4
